To me it seems more logical to pay someone for their productivity, rather than their hours. It gives the workers more interest in the success of the business.

I've always scratched my head at this. Is there something wrong with co-ops or is it just the aggressive simplicity of capital investment that keeps it so dominant?
It's alright for routine business, not very good for high risk/high growth companies. Coordination problems and labor relations are also an issue.

But why? If you set up the power structure to act more like a corporation where a CEO and other executives have unlimited power in some or most decisions, then surely the co-op wouldn't get bogged down by bureaucratic or democratic procedures.
Most workers don't want profit sharing or delayed payments. They want their money now.
